held.counterparty_cb: Asian Clearing Union (member central banks and monetary authorities)
held.source_title: Asian Clearing Union — 'Introduction' (membership list and objectives)
held.note: The ACU's own introduction page lists its member central banks and gives as one of its objectives the provision of a currency swap arrangement among participants. The host resets curl connections (three attempts, all 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer'), so the page was read with the fetch tool rather than as raw HTML. For that reason no amount, date or term is claimed in this record — only membership, and the arrangement's stated swap objective. Note that an ACU swap objective is not evidence that any particular member has drawn or that a bilateral line exists.
held._held_reason: HELD FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, either of which would be enough. FIRST, THE SOURCE CANNOT BE READ: asianclearingunion.org resets the connection to every scripted request, three of three for the researching agent and nine of nine for the merge script, so the membership list was read only through the fetch tool. Round 74 established that a fetch summary is not evidence, and round 75 held a Mauritian and a Salvadoran record on the same ground. SECOND, AND MORE FUNDAMENTAL, THIS MAY NOT BE THIS ROW'S INSTRUMENT AT ALL. The Asian Clearing Union is a mechanism for settling trade between member countries, not a swap or repo line between central banks. Filing ten members on it would have put a different instrument on the row under the same colour — which is exactly the reasoning the agent itself used, correctly, to refuse the Arab Monetary Fund, whose lending goes to governments and finance ministries rather than to central banks. The same test refuses this. If the owner wants clearing-union membership on the map it is a sound thing to record, but as its own relation with its own wording, not as a swap line.
